findings.where: the feeling row in the Chat thread — the note reading 'a squeeze' at 08 frame 300 and at 07 frame 260
findings.what: The same thread row is drawn two ways inside one evidence set: measuring the note's left edge on the half-resolution frame, it starts at x=59 in 08_state_propagating.mp4 and at x=74 in 07_feeling_landing.mp4 (right edge x=441 in both), and the feeling's name is overrun by the object's stem in 08 and in evidence/.previous/07_feeling_landing.mp4 but is clear of it in the re-shot 07 — MANIFEST.json explains why, recording 14 of the 15 present artifacts as from_this_run:false, 13 of them byte-identical to the previous capture (DIFF.json ssim 1.0).
findings.why: The row is scored on one visual language holding across all five regions, and the set on the glass shows one component in two states because only one artifact was re-shot; a reader comparing two clips of the same region sees two builds, not one system.

findings.what: There is no Android artifact anywhere in the set and no APK anywhere on disk, so the clause 'both platforms serve the same regions, the same feelings, and the same event types' is carried entirely by the source (one lib/, one app.dart naming the five regions, 270 lines of Kotlin in four files for widget, haptics and ambient only, ten platform-branch lines in the whole of lib/) and never by a picture; the reason given is measured rather than asserted — no /dev/kvm, adbd up at 113 minutes with no package service behind it, no GTK, and a Flutter-tester probe that rendered flat fills — so it is a reason and not an excuse, but it is still an unphotographed half.
findings.why: The last clause of the row asks about both platforms, and half of it can only be read in the code, which caps how far the artifacts alone can carry this category.

findings.where: 04_moments.png: the video tile at approx (60,2380)-(470,2560) reading '2s', beside the voice note in the same band reading '0:52'. 14_media_viewer.png: the film strip at approx y=2170-2320 reading '0:01 / 0:03'
findings.what: The app writes a duration in two grammars and rounds it two ways: logs/14_media_viewer.report.json records duration_ms 2500 and the viewer shows '0:03', while the Moments tile badge truncates — app/lib/regions/moments/moments_region.dart:622 uses `~/ 1000` where every other duration site (moments_region.dart:574, thread/renderers.dart:72, regions/chat/blob_widgets.dart:372) uses `(ms/1000).round()` — so a 2.5-second video reads '2s' in one region and '0:03' in another, and inside 04_moments.png alone a voice note's length reads '0:52' next to a video's '2s'.
findings.why: The row asks that the same event read the same wherever it appears; two roundings and two formats for one fact is the one visual language failing in a small way that is visible in a single frame.

findings.where: the pairing card under THE TWO PHONES, against the banner above it
findings.what: The card reads 'not paired yet · LINK connecting' while the banner above it carries the partner's standing line ('week one, and the room smells right …', travelling, need and energy dials) and logs/reception.report.json records 14062 events and cursor 14061 on that device — a phone holding a year of two-person history and saying it has never been paired.
findings.why: Every region being a view onto the one log means the regions should not contradict each other about whether there is a partner; this is in a scene that logs/reception.json is explicit is not one of the seventeen artifacts, which is why it is minor.

findings.what: The registry's own header says 'docs/EVENT_TYPES.md lists the same seventeen types' while kEventTypes holds eighteen (measured: 18 `id:` entries) and docs/EVENT_TYPES.md is titled 'Adding a nineteenth'; the schema test that holds the registry and the doc equal passes, so only the prose is stale.
findings.why: The single registry is the thing every module and both platforms are held to, and a count in it that no longer matches is the one place a reader would take the number from.

what_is_working: One log, measured five ways rather than asserted. Every region's report in the same run carries the same event count and the same sync cursor — 14062 in logs/01_pulse, 02_chat, 03_us, 04_moments, 05_settings and 12_search .report.json — and the arrivals in logs/08_state_propagating.json show a state change, a feeling and a message each advancing that one counter by exactly one (8082 to 8083 to 8084 to 8085 to 8086 to 8087). evidence/reliability.json: events_host 174, events_client 174, duplicates 0, same_order_both_sides true, ordering monotonic, typing 'neither log grew by it', a reaction 'folded onto the target, not a row', an edit with 'original kept in the log'. evidence/coldstart.json: spine_host_order and spine_client_order identical over four events.

The same event appears in two regions with the same name and the same clock. In 08_state_propagating.mp4 the feeling 'hold' lands on Pulse at frame 16 and is then found in the Chat thread at frames 165-190 as the same object labelled 'hold / Thu 3 Sep · 20:41'. In 07_feeling_landing.mp4 'a squeeze' settles into the Pulse row at frame 220 reading '19:45 · noor' and appears in the Chat thread at frame 221 reading 'a squeeze / Thu 3 Sep · 19:45'. In the stills, 01_pulse.png's row reads 'empty chair 17:19' and 13_messenger_states.png's thread reads 'empty chair / Thu 3 Sep · 17:19 · read', and logs/01_pulse.report.json gives that event id 0001M4GW48FEW3M67XKAZT5051 at ts 1788455973000, which is 17:19 UTC to the minute.

The Chat thread is a timeline of every kind of event, not a message list. Stepping 11_chat_scroll.mp4 turns up written notes, a photograph with a caption, feelings ('thinking of you', 'goodnight', 'miss you', 'nyeh'), state lines from both people ('noor got in', 'you are heads down', "noor's phone is on silent", 'you · home'), and a to-do row with a checkbox and read marks ('the pressure at hers again … back on the list · Mon 27 Apr · 18:26 read'). logs/13_messenger_states.report.json counts the visible rows as {feeling: 1, state_declared: 1, message: 5}, which is what the picture shows.

Search is one index over the one log, and its facets are generated from the registry. logs/12_search.report.json records the query 'rain' returning kinds {message: 8, ritual_kept: 1, todo_event: 1} — a ritual and a to-do sitting in the same result list as eight messages — and 12_search.png shows chips for EVERYTHING, WRITTEN, PHOTOGRAPHS, VIDEO, TALKING, FEELINGS, STATE and then exactly the five module labels, DATES, TO DO, DATES THAT MATTER, RITUALS, THE SHELF. In the source that chip list is `for (final m in kModules) m.label: m.eventTypes` (app/lib/regions/chat/search_page.dart:61), so a sixth module brings its own chip.

Partner state is on every screen, and it is one component: the top 180 rows of 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 12 and 13 are pixel-identical (mean |difference| 0.000, share of pixels differing by more than 8 grey levels 0.00%). The two unpaired stills, 10_first_run.png and 17_setup_pwa.png, are identical to each other and carry the same band saying 'nothing from them yet. the six words are on the other phone.' 14_media_viewer.png is the only screen without it, and it is a full-screen overlay.

One chrome across the regions: the tab strip band (rows 2960-3120) is byte-identical between 02_chat.png, 12_search.png, 10_first_run.png and 17_setup_pwa.png (max difference 0.0) and differs from 01_pulse.png only by which tab is raised (mean 12.7, 32% of pixels). crops/dusk_pulse.png is the same Pulse layout under the second light with the same six feelings at the same six times.

State propagates into the chrome, not just into one card. In 08_state_propagating.mp4 the far side declares 'state mood restless' at frame 0 and the Pulse card reads 'restless' by frame 8; it declares 'state place out' at frame 411 and the standing banner changes from 'TRAVELLING NEED ||| ENERGY |' to 'OUT NEED ||| ENERGY |' from frame 415 to the end — and by then the region on screen is Us, so the change is legible on a screen that is not Pulse.

Feelings land in every region, not only Pulse. 07_feeling_landing.mp4 shows one arriving on Pulse (frames 0-220), one in Chat (frames 221-313) and one on Us (frames 314-420); 15_authored_feeling.mp4 shows the picker opened from Us, and the authored feeling landing on Us, then on Pulse, then on Settings. logs/haptics.check.json counts 36 feelings, 34 built in and 2 authored, in six families, with 36 distinct haptic strings and no near-shapes; crops/haptics_strip.png names them and the families match the picker sheet in 15 exactly.

An authored feeling travels the same path as a built-in one: logs/07_feeling_landing.json's fourth arrival is 'feeling soup 0.85' with logs/07_feeling_landing.sound.json placing assets/sound/snd_user_soup.ogg at its frame, the same shape of record as the three built-in arrivals before it, and logs/05_settings.report.json counts authored_feelings: 2. logs/surfaces.json reports 34 feeling objects named and 'named_but_neither': [] — no feeling without a surface.

Settings is a view onto the registry rather than a hand-written list: its interrupt rows read 'something written / a picture / something to watch / their voice / an answer to something of yours / a feeling / something they say about themselves / something their phone notices / a date moving', which is the `announced` field of app/lib/spine/types.dart in registry order with the three Notify.none types skipped. A new event type gets its Settings row without anyone writing one.

The extensibility claim is enforced rather than described, and I checked it by grep and by running the tests. Each module's event type appears only inside its own directory plus one entry in the spine registry (date_event: 10 hits in lib/modules/dates/ and 1 in lib/spine/types.dart; todo_event 10 and 1; milestone 6 and 2; ritual_kept 7 and 1; passed_on 7 and 1) and each module's id appears outside its directory only as a search facet in that same registry. kModules is iterated generically at every shared site — the thread renderer table (lib/thread/renderers.dart:179), the paper assignment (lib/material/assignment.dart:35), the Us desk budget (lib/regions/us/us_region.dart:42,85,86,91,93), the search facets and the capture hooks. `flutter test test/module_costs_test.dart test/persistence_boundary_test.dart test/spine_schema_test.dart test/thread_types_test.dart` — 17 tests, all passed. Five shared-life modules already ship on this contract, which is one more than the row asks to be possible.

No second store, and it is guarded: lib/spine/store/ is the only directory that imports a driver (sqlite3 in store_sqlite.dart, IndexedDB in store_web.dart) and test/persistence_boundary_test.dart fails the build if anything outside lib/spine/ imports one — it passes. A separate run of test/spine_replay_golden_test.dart and test/every_module_is_on_the_desk_test.dart (10 tests, all passed) includes 'every module reads the same log and says something from it', 'order of arrival does not decide the view; seq does' and 'a read marker moves a mark and is never a row'.

One codebase for both platforms: app/lib/app.dart names PulseRegion, ChatRegion, UsRegion, MomentsRegion and SettingsRegion once, at lines 258-262; the whole of lib/ contains ten lines that branch on platform, across four files, and eight conditional-import shims; android/ carries four Kotlin files totalling 270 lines for the widget, the haptics and the ambient channel, and no second UI. crops/reception_open.png shows the same Pulse region reflowed into a desktop Chromium window with the same tab strip and the same standing banner.

verdict: This is one system, and I could measure that rather than infer it. Five regions report the same event count and the same sync cursor in the same run; a state change, a feeling and a message pushed from the far side each move that one counter by exactly one; a feeling that lands on Pulse is found in the Chat thread under the same name at the same minute (hold, 20:41, in 08; a squeeze, 19:45, in 07; empty chair, 17:19, across 01_pulse.png and 13_messenger_states.png); the thread carries photographs, voice, feelings, both people's state lines and a to-do row with a checkbox; one search over the log returns a ritual and a to-do beside eight messages; and the Settings interrupt list is the event-type registry's own words in registry order. The extensibility half is stronger than the row asks: five shared-life modules already ship on one contract, each module's event types and id appear nowhere outside its own directory except in the single spine registry (measured by grep, five for five), every shared site iterates kModules generically, and the tests that hold this — module_costs_test, persistence_boundary_test, spine_schema_test, thread_types_test, spine_replay_golden_test — pass when run. One store: lib/spine/store/ is the only place a driver is imported and the build fails if that changes. What keeps this off full marks is not the architecture but what is on the glass. Fourteen of the fifteen present artifacts were not shot in this capture and thirteen are byte-identical to the previous one, and the single re-shot clip differs visibly from the rest in how a feeling row is drawn — so the set itself shows one component two ways, which is exactly the failure the row is written against, arriving through the capture rather than through the design. Beyond that: no Android artifact exists at all, so half of the both-platforms clause can only be read in the source; the app writes a video's length as '2s' in Moments and '0:03' in the viewer from two different roundings in two files; and a non-artifact crop shows a phone holding fourteen thousand events saying it has never been paired. None of these is structural. Thirteen of fifteen: the architecture is coherent and genuinely extensible, and the evidence for it is one capture behind itself.
